label: early original-phase x/f/0 (also e/r/n) input in sequences starting with v/u/d/k
explanation: Fires almost only during the original phase (98.5% of activation mass), at original positions 2-6 and mostly 3-4. It never fires at t=0-1, in the copy phase, or at t>=7, and only weakly on <DEL>. The input token is the main driver: x (8.3x lift), f and 0 (about 7x), then e, r and n (about 2x); digit 1 and j almost never fire it. It fires mostly on the first occurrence of the token. Activation is boosted when the first original token is v, u, d or k (about 3-4x lift), and less so for s, b, w or 2. The top activations look like v/u/d + two letters + x/f/0 at t=3-4. Restricting to t 3-4 with input in {x,f,0,e,r,n} and a first token in {v,u,d,k,s,b,w,2} gives dev F1 about 0.51 (precision 0.59, mass recall 0.61). Widening to t 2-5 raises mass recall to 0.73 but costs precision. Much of the variance looks like a graded sum of input identity and the earlier context, so a boolean predicate gets only about half of it.
